subject: Post-demo: Caravel integration, routing policies, SDK auth & next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@caravel.ai>, Noah Kim <noah.kim@caravel.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo recap & technical follow-ups (Caravel)

Hi Elena / Noah —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap from our side and the technical asks we captured so we can keep momentum: 

Key goals you mentioned:
- Low-latency chat for customer support (95th pct < 300ms for short queries)
- Reranker over product catalog embeddings for relevance tuning
- Region-aware routing (US primary, EU for GDPR-bound EU customers)
- Audit trails / retention controls for support transcripts

Top technical items we promised to follow up on:
1) SDK & auth: sample SDK initialization with token rotation + short-lived creds for your support agents.
2) Model routing: suggested policy draft that routes interactive traffic to a fast TPU/quantized variant, with fallback to a higher-quality model only on quality regression.
3) Structured output/tool-calling: example schema for order lookup tool-calls and embedding-based reranker hooks.
4) Embeddings & rerankers: proposed embedding dimension, indexing strategy, and approximate recall targets.

I've looped in Rishi and Dev to propose specific configs and a quick T/T for an internal P0 test. Marcus will weigh in on cost/throughput estimates.

Next meeting: suggest a 30-min technical alignment early next week to lock the SDK auth flow and routing policy.

Attachments: caravel-demo-notes.pdf (your annotated deck).

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <elena@caravel.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Noah Kim <noah.kim@caravel.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & technical follow-ups (Caravel)

Tessa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side so the alignment call is productive: 
- For the reranker: we plan to start with 384-d vectors (FAISS HNSW). Target 95% recall@50 on our validation set.
- Auth: we prefer short-lived tokens tied to our IdP (Okta) and would like a sample for rotating keys upstream.
- Tool calling: we need guaranteed exactly-once semantics for order lookup calls (idempotency token approach).

Would also appreciate an outline of routing policy behavior under congestion (e.g., if fast model saturates — what gets routed to fallback and what gets throttled).

Availability: Mon 12/7 morning PT works for our engineers.

—Elena
VP Product, Caravel AI

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@caravel.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T13:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & technical follow-ups (Caravel) — preliminary config + SDK snippet

Elena / team —

Following up with concrete tech notes ahead of Monday so we can hit the ground running: 

1) SDK & auth (attached: redwood-sdk-auth-snippet.patch)
- Pattern: exchange Okta OIDC assertion at your backend -> call Redwood private token endpoint -> receive short-lived inference token (TTL 5m).
- Sample header: Authorization: Bearer <short_lived_token>
- Rotation: rotate signing key weekly; support key-id in token header to enable smooth rollovers.

2) Embeddings / reranker\- Recommendation: 384 dims, nprobes=8 for ANN during dev, scale to nprobes=16 for production if recall drops. Store per-customer namespaces for GDPR scoping.

3) Routing policy (suggested draft)
- Route rules (priority order):
  a) Region pin: if request.customer_region == "eu" -> EU cluster (model-eu-small).
  b) Latency SLO: prefer fast-quantized model (model-fq-8bit) if observed p95 <= 250ms for last 5m window.
  c) Cost override: if budget-tag == "dev" -> route to lower-cost distil variant.
  d) Fallback chain: model-fq-8bit -> model-baseline-quant -> model-highquality (warm cold start allowed).
- Congestion behavior: when pool saturation >80% for primary model, shift new requests to next tier for non-priority customers; for priority=true (support agents) keep requests queued up to 500ms, then route to fallback.

4) Structured output/tool-calls\- Suggest schema for order lookup:
  {"tool":"order_lookup","input":{"order_id":"string"},"response_schema":{"status":"enum","items":"list"}}
- Idempotency: include client-provided idempotency_key; server should store 24h TTL.

I've attached a short patch with the SDK init example. Marcus will follow with cost/throughput estimates.

Thanks —
Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Elena Torres <elena@caravel.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & technical follow-ups (Caravel) — cost & SLO note

Elena / team —

A few cost/throughput numbers to set expectations (ballpark, will refine after trial):
- model-fq-8bit (quantized fast): ~ $0.28 per 1k tokens generated, p95 gen latency ~ 120-220ms depending on prompt length.
- model-baseline-quant: ~ $0.45 per 1k tokens, p95 ~ 250-400ms.
- model-highquality: ~ $1.10 per 1k tokens, p95 > 400ms typically.

Routing policy impact: if 30% of traffic hits fallback on average, expect ~+18% unit cost; if we can keep fallback <10% via autoscaling, cost impact ~+6%.

Throughput: a single dedicated pool (A100 x8) sustains ~450 concurrent interactive sessions with our continuous batching heuristics — enough for a small-to-medium support org, but we should size by peak concurrency.

Actionable ask for the Monday call: confirm priority flag semantics (who is priority=true) and whether you want strict region isolation for EU data (logical vs physical).

Attachments: routing-policy-estimates.xlsx (simple sheet with cost scenarios).

—Marcus
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & technical follow-ups (Caravel) — next steps and owners

Team —

Thanks everyone for the quick turn. Consolidated next steps and owners: 
- Monday 12/7 10:00 PT: Technical alignment call (30m) — Tessa (host), Dev (SDK/auth), Marcus (routing/cost), Elena + Noah (Caravel eng).
- Dev: prepare a runnable SDK snippet + short-lived token flow (deadline: 12/6 EOD). Attachment: redwood-sdk-auth-snippet.patch.
- Marcus: finalize cost scenarios and a recommended concurrency-sizing doc (deadline: 12/8). Attachment: routing-policy-estimates.xlsx.
- Rishi: coordinate SOW/PO path and initial trial terms; will propose a 6-week POC + 30k token/day cap (deadline: 12/9).
- Elena / Caravel: share a small validation set for reranker (5k queries) and confirm priority user list & EU data scope (deadline: 12/8).

I'll create the HubSpot task and share the calendar invite for the alignment call. If anything above is off, flag now — otherwise we'll proceed with the timeline.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
